description.fun: A tidy duckling whose feathers secrete a glossy gel that repels water and grime, keeping its coif smooth. It hates getting dirty, especially on its head, and it tends to overthink things. Its strong legs let it swim easily even in fast rivers. Unlike every other first partner, its kind isn't native: Quaxly migrated to Paldea from distant lands long ago.
description.guide: The Water-type first partner Pokémon of Paldea, from Pokémon Scarlet and Violet. Quaxly's gel-coated feathers repel water and dirt, and its legs make it a strong swimmer. It evolves into Quaxwell and then Quaquaval.
description.tagline: A neat-freak duckling with a gelled coif

description.fun: A hard-working dancer in training. Quaxwell studies the moves of people and Pokémon from many regions and works them into its routines, and flocks run through shallow water to train their legs, then compete for the most graceful kick. Its crest absorbs blows, but if it gets messed up, Quaxwell feels out of sorts until it combs it back into shape with gel.
description.guide: The middle stage of Quaxly's line. Quaxwell trains its legs constantly and adds dance moves from people and Pokémon of other regions to its routines.
description.tagline: A dancer in training who can't stand a messy crest

description.fun: A dancing duck whose single kick can send a truck rolling. Quaquaval dances in styles from far-off lands, mesmerizing all who watch, while decorative water feathers fan out from its tail and spin around it to slice into foes. Even asleep, it sways and strikes elegant poses. Its look draws on carnival dancers like those of Rio and Tenerife, and its kicks on capoeira.
description.guide: The final evolution of Quaxly and Paldea's Water-type first partner, a Water and Fighting-type Pokémon inspired by carnival dancers. Its water feathers slice into foes as it dances.
description.tagline: A carnival dancer whose kicks can send a truck rolling
